headline: Targets: 4 of 4 measurable targets move as the catalogs predict. Not measurable: R Draconis (saturated).

Other stars: 65 of 73 Gaia stars the tool was never tuned on move exactly as Gaia predicts (4 fields). 81% of their measurements fall within 1 error bar and 95% within 2, against 68% and 95% for honest error bars.

Positions: allowing for crowding, 75% of star positions fall within 1 error bar of Gaia and 89% within 2 (81% and 98% for stars with no close neighbour). 59 of 73 stars have a neighbour within 2 pixels, which shifts their light centre slightly; this never fakes motion.
Measured targets sit within 0.61 arcsec of their catalog positions (at most 0.1 of a pixel), a constant shift that can't create motion.

method.motion: Measured vs catalog motion per axis, z = difference / error; combined chi-square with 2 degrees of freedom. Agrees if p >= 0.05, tension if 0.0027 <= p < 0.05, disagrees if p < 0.0027 (3 sigma).
method.error_bars: Pull = (measured - expected position) / error bar. Honest error bars put 68% of pulls within 1 and 95% within 2.
method.field_stars: Gaia stars in the field, excluding stars used to set the error bars, stars merged with a neighbour, and saturated visits. Motion test (main): each star's constant offset is removed, then its visits are tested against Gaia's predicted motion. Position test: distance from Gaia's position, with an extra allowance for the constant shift crowding causes (measured on the reference stars).
method.not_scored: Field-star brightness, objects in no catalog, and motion of saturated targets.
